name: Chicken Tikka
description: Smoky Pakistani chicken tikka marinated in yogurt, lemon, ginger-garlic and spices, then grilled over strong heat for juicy pieces with charred edges.
ingredients: 800 g boneless chicken, cut into similar-size pieces
method: Pat the chicken dry and cut it into similar-size pieces so they cook at roughly the same rate.
Mix the yogurt, lemon juice, ginger-garlic paste, red chilli, cumin, coriander, garam masala, oil and salt into a smooth marinade.
Coat the chicken thoroughly, cover and marinate in the refrigerator for at least 2 hours. Keep raw chicken chilled throughout marination.
Thread the pieces onto skewers with a little space between them, or arrange them in a single layer on a grill rack so heat can circulate.

Grill over medium-high to high heat, turning as needed, until the exterior has charred spots and the thickest pieces are fully cooked. Use a reliable doneness check rather than judging by surface colour alone.
Rest the cooked tikka for a few minutes, then serve hot with mint chutney, sliced onion and lemon.
tips: Keep the chicken pieces similar in size so they finish cooking together.
Do not reuse marinade that has contacted raw chicken as a serving sauce unless it has been thoroughly cooked first.
Avoid repeatedly cutting every piece open during grilling, which releases juices and makes consistent cooking harder.
storage: Cool leftovers promptly, refrigerate covered, and reheat only the portion you plan to serve until thoroughly hot.
image_alt: Pakistani chicken tikka with charred spiced chicken pieces served hot on a platter
image_caption: Charred Pakistani chicken tikka photographed as the main dish rather than as part of a mixed grill.
technique: The marinade should coat rather than drip off the chicken. Pat the pieces dry first, use thick yogurt, give the marinade at least two chilled hours, and space the pieces on skewers so hot air or grill heat can reach their sides.
doneness_cues: Marinated chicken should carry a visible coating without a puddle of thin yogurt at the bottom.
The exterior should develop charred spots while the centre remains juicy.
The thickest pieces must be fully cooked; surface colour alone is not a safe doneness test.
Rested tikka should release some juice but not raw-looking liquid.
mistakes: Using watery yogurt and a wet chicken surface so the marinade slides off.
Cutting pieces in very different sizes.
Packing skewers so tightly that sides steam instead of brown.
Using leftover raw-chicken marinade as a table sauce without cooking it thoroughly.
substitutions: Boneless thigh stays forgiving on high heat; breast can be used but needs closer timing.
Reduce red chilli without changing lemon, cumin and coriander.
For an oven grill, use a rack so released moisture can fall away from the chicken.
reheating: Reheat briefly and covered or in a hot oven only until thoroughly hot; long reheating dries grilled chicken.
serving: Serve with mint chutney, onion rings and lemon immediately after the short rest.

faqs.question: Why does tikka marinade fall off?
faqs.answer: The chicken or yogurt is probably too wet, or the marinade did not have enough chilled time to adhere. Pat chicken dry and use thicker yogurt.

faqs.question: How long should chicken tikka marinate?
faqs.answer: This recipe uses at least 2 hours in the refrigerator. Keep raw chicken chilled throughout marination.

faqs.question: How do I get char without drying the chicken?
faqs.answer: Use strong heat, evenly sized pieces and enough spacing, then stop once the thickest pieces are fully cooked.
